close_reason: Decision-type finding: ratifies the bench file's separation of bench_parse_* and bench_convert_* modes (with parse output hoisted out of the convert inner loop) for regression localization. The design is documented in the bench file structure itself and the file-level doc comment. No code change required; finding records the rationale for future contributors who might be tempted to collapse them.
description:
Why this choice is correct: crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs deliberately runs parse and convert as separate bench functions (bench_parse_* and bench_convert_*) with the parse output hoisted out of the inner loop of the convert benches (lines 333-370). This lets a future regression be localized to one of two layers:

- bench_parse_* regression → mime-tree's parse() got slower.
- bench_convert_* regression → jmap-mime's message_to_jmap_body got slower.

A naive bench design would only measure 'parse + convert end-to-end'. That measurement cannot tell the operator which layer regressed. The separation here is the difference between a bench that surfaces actionable information and one that just says 'something is slower'.

A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' by deleting bench_parse_* on the grounds that the pipeline mode covers the same ground. That suggestion should be rejected on the localization argument above. (Note: the sibling efficiency finding JMAP-t307.3 recommends deleting bench_pipeline_*, not the separated benches — those should stay.)

Also worth defending: convert_only's parse-once-outside-the-loop is the correct microbenchmark idiom for isolating the cost of just the adapter walk. Do not 'fix' that by moving parse back inside b.iter().
title: Bench separates parse-only and convert-only modes for regression localization
